note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about this oven, dryer or fryer exhaust routing, recovery already provided and any unresolved own-inlet or process-use basis?

evidence.text: equipment D-A reads "D-A Product dryer A"
stream EX-A (asset stream:EX-A) reads "Dryer A exhaust"
equipment HX-A reads "HX-A Exhaust heat recovery exchanger"
HX-A enabled = false; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-A source_revision = "A"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-A coverage_claim = "not operating"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-A observed_hours = 0; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-A bypass_status = "bypassed"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-A cause = "unknown"; blank; meaning and suitability unverified

data_requests.item: Existing exhaust routing and represented recovery coverage for this unit
where: site records: approved existing drawings, routing/configuration and recovery-purpose records for the identified unit, including revision, source locator, owner and any supplied full, partial, shared or unknown coverage claim
maintenance records: existing recovery availability, bypass, fault, inspection and cleaning records for the represented equipment
data_requests.how: Distinguish recovery already provided from an unresolved residual question. A represented item, document label or enabled flag is a candidate, not authenticated operation or complete coverage. A shared recoverer does not establish a duty allocation; a missing drawn item does not prove absent hardware.

data_requests.item: Existing exhaust-condition, product and maintenance basis
where: site records: permitted existing exhaust temperature/flow, moisture, contaminants and representative production records with unit identity, quantity, location, units, method, dates and operating-period basis
maintenance records: existing product carry-over, filtration, fouling, leakage, cleaning and pressure-loss observations relevant to the identified exhaust path
data_requests.how: Review whether the available records represent this job. Preserve unknown, zero and disabled qualifiers and product/moisture restrictions. Any missing-data plan belongs to the responsible reviewer; no new measurement task or fixed observation duration is prescribed.

data_requests.item: Existing heat-input, operating-period and comparison basis
where: site records: approved existing fuel or heat-input and production/run schedules for a justified comparison period, with equipment identity, dates and stated basis
utility bills or the site energy report: existing identified sub-meter or heat-supply records, if suitable for the selected unit and production basis
data_requests.how: Separate a recorded nameplate/input from actual representative operation. No universal minimum hours, mandatory month, recovery fraction or savings is inferred. Qualified review can decide that existing coverage or documented constraints settle or defer the job.

data_requests.item: Own-inlet or process-use alternatives and constraints for qualified review
where: site records: existing own-inlet/process heat-use, layout/duct/piping space, product quality, moisture, contaminant and operating-constraint records, including options already assessed
the vendor datasheet: applicable equipment requirements and documented direct/indirect recovery constraints and the receiving engineering owner
data_requests.how: S26 describes indirect circulating-medium/run-around recovery as an option when local duct space is limited; assess applicability rather than treating lack of nearby direct-duct space as universal closure. It is not an automatic recommendation or feasibility result. H6 separately asks about a named external duty.

questions.decision_rule: Use qualified existing records to distinguish working full coverage, unavailable or partial recovery and unresolved own-inlet/process-use questions. A responsible engineer can answer or defer the investigation from an adequate documented basis; no new project is compulsory. Consider applicable direct and indirect alternatives and product, cleanliness, moisture, safety and operating constraints before deciding whether further assessment is worthwhile. Missing local duct space or intermittent operation alone is not an automatic universal closure.

typical_benefit.wording: Dryers (S26, p. 104): "A simple form of heat recovery in retrofit applications is to utilize the exhaust air of a dryer to preheat the inlet air stream, thereby saving energy." Spray dryers (S25, p. 90): "It is estimated that up to 30% of the heat from the dryer exhaust can be recovered." Fryers (S26, p. 107): "Conditioning of the exhaust gas is required, however, to remove fats and to reduce fouling of the heat exchange system." No source in this set gives a figure for ovens.
source_titles: S26: Masanet, Worrell, Graus and Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Fruit and Vegetable Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-59289-Revision, Mar 2008)

S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: S26 printed p.104 discusses dryer recovery options and humidity limits; S25 printed p.90 discusses contaminated dairy-dryer exhaust. Applying these examples to other supplied equipment requires qualified review. Showing represented coverage and retaining unresolved residual/maintenance questions is authored records-review policy, not proof of missing hardware, available heat or a required retrofit. A supplied fully-covered working claim may settle new-opportunity triage after company review; if shown, it is acknowledged as existing coverage, not asserted absent. Company engineering/product/safety review governs any actual exhaust or equipment work.
